requirements.definition: rst is an active-high asynchronous reset that clears button sampling history, control state, mode, both timers, and divider remainders; both timer values become zero, and the scan index becomes zero. During reset, LED bits directly driven by switches still follow sw.

The four buttons are sampled once every 100000 source clock rising edges; each button must be 1 for 8 consecutive samples to generate one event. Holding a button does not repeat the event; at least one low sample followed by another 8 high samples is required to retrigger.

The initial state enters stopwatch stopped when sw[1]=0; it enters clock running when sw[1]=1 and sw[2]=0, and waits if both are 1. In stopwatch stopped, sw[1] has priority to enter clock mode, followed by R to enter running, then L to enter a single-cycle clear-to-zero state, then D to enter a single-cycle direction-toggle state. Stopwatch running accepts only sw[1] to switch to clock mode or R to stop; L/D have no effect. The clear-to-zero and direction states return to stopped after one cycle.

While the stopwatch is running, one registered tick is generated every 1000000 enabled source edges, and the next source edge advances the time by one hundredth of a second. Time spans 24 hours × 60 minutes × 60 seconds × 100 hundredths of a second, with incrementing carrying through successive fields; in reverse, borrowing propagates from 0 through successive fields to 23:59:59.99. Stopping freezes the divider remainder, and clearing clears the remainder; for each digit, tick takes priority over clear on the same edge.

The clock runs autonomously in all non-editing control states, generating a registered tick every 1000000 enabled edges and counting hundredths of a second on the following edge. In W_RUN, sw[1]=0 is handled first to return to stopwatch stopped; otherwise, sw[2]=1 enters editing of the seconds units digit. In an editing state, sw[2]=0 returns to W_RUN; sw[1] does not directly cause an exit during editing. Editing freezes the clock divider remainder.

The editing cursor order is seconds units, seconds tens, minutes units, minutes tens, and hours; L moves forward and R backward, with wraparound, and L takes priority over R. U increments the current digit by 1, and D decrements it by 1, with U taking priority over D; seconds/minutes units are modulo 10, tens are modulo 6, and hours are modulo 24, with no carry or borrow between digits during editing. For a digit that actually receives tick, tick takes priority over editing.

led[0]=sw[0], led[1]=sw[1], led[2]=sw[1]&!sw[2], led[3]=sw[1]&sw[2]; led4 corresponds to minutes units, led5 to minutes tens, led6 to seconds units or hours, and led7 to seconds tens; the cursor LEDs are off in other control states.

The display combinationally selects the stopwatch or clock corresponding to sw[1]. The scan index resets to 0, reaches 1 after the first 50000 source edges, and then increments by 1 modulo 8 every 100000 edges. fnd_com follows the sequence 1110/1101/1011/0111 based only on the low 2 bits of the index. Indices 0/1 display hundredths-of-a-second units/tens (sw0=0) or minutes units/tens (sw0=1); 2/3 display seconds units/tens or hours units/tens; 4/5/7 are blank, and 6 displays a dot when hundredths of a second <=50 and is blank when >50.
